Date: Thu, 20 Apr 2028 15:05:00 +0000
Subject: Private fleet safeguard scenarios and decision tree

Claire / GH ops team —

Following up on our pre-upgrade alignment call: attached is a first-pass decision tree (DecisionTree_v1.pdf) that maps milestone gates for a Private fleet minor version refresh (v4.2.1 -> v4.3.0). The goal is to reduce blast radius while keeping the maintenance window under 6 hours.

Key asks from us to you:
- Confirm the maintenance window you prefer for the upgrade: proposed UTC window is 2028-05-03 00:00–06:00 UTC.
- Any blackout periods we should avoid for Greenfield Health?
- Who'll be the ops owner on your side for the dry-run?

Highlights in the decision tree: canary gating at 5% / 25% / 100%, KV-cache drain before canary, network cordon and egress rule changes, post-upgrade validation checks (latency, error rate, KV hit ratio). Fallback options include: immediate shelfing of the hotpatch, rollback to pinned version v4.2.1, and an emergency circuit-breaker to redirect traffic to Hosted.

Attached: DecisionTree_v1.pdf (diagram + decision matrix).

If this window works I’ll schedule a dry-run for April 30 and propose owners for each step.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the diagram, looks thorough. May 3 UTC window is acceptable on our side; the only constraint is no database schema jobs between 01:00–02:00 UTC that day. Ops owner will be me (Claire Nguyen) plus SRE on call (platform-ops).

- Please confirm the KV-cache drain script idempotency — we cannot accept a partial drain that leaves stale keys for more than 5 minutes.
- If you plan a Hosted fallback, we need a read-only mode on the application to avoid write inconsistencies.

I’ll loop in our security lead if we need deeper evidence.

Subject: Re: Private fleet safeguard scenarios and decision tree

Claire / team —

Short answers and technical artifacts:
- KV-cache drain: we’ll run the drain in two phases — soft drain (stop new write-allocations, migrate hot keys) then hard drain (evict remaining keys). The soft drain is safe and idempotent; script is dry-runable. I attached a short snippet to the runbook. Hard drain includes a verification hook that samples 1000 keys and confirms TTL==0.
- Canary gating: propose 5% (10 hosts) for 30m with health checks (p90 latency, 5xx rate <0.5%), 25% for 45m with extended telemetry, then 100%. Canary fire/rollback automated via our orchestration: if checks fail we run the shelf action (pin fleet to v4.2.1) and rollback migrations.
- Network cordon: implementation will add an iptables reject for new traffic + BGP withdraw on a per-rack basis to speed isolation if needed. We can revert BGP in <3m.

Operational requirements for GH:
1) A test client that can replay production read/write profiles during dry-run (we can provide).
2) A person who can approve the canary step within 10 minutes (CLI auth).
3) A monitoring hook that can trigger the circuit-breaker to Hosted.

I’ll add the exact CLI commands to the dryrun-checklist.md.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

- Data residency: no customer payloads leave your VPC unless you approve the Hosted fallback; fallback will be read-only for writes by default.
